nodes.name: Cu substrate preparation
nodes.procedure: Bulky Cu substrate was polished successively with sandpaper of 1000#, 1500# and 2000# grits, then soaked in acetone for 5 min to degrease before electrodeposition.
nodes.source_text: bulky Cu substrate was polished successively with sandpaper of 1000#, 1500# and 2000# grits, then soaked in acetone for 5 min to degrease

nodes.name: Surface activation
nodes.procedure: Then Cu substrate was immersed in 5 wt% HCl solution at room temperature for 5 min to remove oxide film for surface activation.
nodes.source_text: Cu substrate was immersed in 5 wt% HCl solution at room temperature for 5 min to remove oxide film

nodes.name: Gradient electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The pH value of electrodeposition solution kept at a constant temperature of 40 °C was adjusted to 4.0 by adding 5 wt% HCl solution. Gradient electrodeposition proceeds in three steps: the deposition is activated for 5 min at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² at first, then for 40 min at 30 mA cm⁻², and for 2 min at 50 mA cm⁻² finally. After the accomplishment of gradient electrodeposition, rapid rinsing with distilled water was necessary to remove residual electrodeposition solution, and the as-fabricated electrode was dried and stored in a dry vessel at room temperature for further performance measurement and microstructure characterization.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-S-Mn deposits show low crystallinity with amorphous structure dominating, containing crystalline Ni₃S₂ and MnS signals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To investigate the phase composition and crystallinity of Ni-S-Mn deposits, an XRD pattern is shown in Fig. 1. It can be intuitively seen that Ni-S-Mn deposits has an expansion of low-intensity diffraction peaks, implying that this Ni-S-Mn deposits has low crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-S-Mn deposits exhibit hierarchical porous morphology like multi-channel wind-erosion-gully with particle sizes of 500-800 nm (large) and 100 nm (small), and flake structures on particle surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By using scanning electron microscope (SEM), the surface morphology and elemental distribution of Ni-S-Mn deposits were investigated. At relatively lower magnification, as shown in Fig. 2a, the Ni-S-Mn deposits presents a hierarchically porous morphology like multi-channel wind-erosion-gully.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni and Mn evenly distributed on Ni-S-Mn deposits surface, S concentrated on surface; higher Mn content on smaller particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In order to explore the elemental composition and distribution on deposits, elemental mapping images and EDS analyses are shown in Fig. 2e and f.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-S-Mn deposits show particles of 100-200 nm with crystalline Ni₃S₂ (lattice spacings 2.34 Å (111), 2.05 Å (202)) and MnS (3.04 Å (101), 3.22 Å (002)) surrounded by amorphous Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further confirm the morphology and microstructure of smaller particles within the Ni-S-Mn deposits, TEM images are shown in Fig. 3. ... it can be clearly identified that the lattice spacings of 3.04 Å and 3.22 Å correspond to the (101) and the (002) planes of MnS, respectively.
